cards.q: What does the IPsec lab configure?
cards.a: It configures site-to-site VPN with IKEv1/v2, transform sets, crypto maps, and interesting traffic, serving as the base VPN skill for DMVPN, FlexVPN, and remote access.

cards.q: What is the IPsec configuration sequence?
cards.a: Configure an isakmp policy, a transform set, an interesting-traffic ACL, a crypto map, then apply it to the interface.

cards.q: What are the differences between IKEv1 and IKEv2?
cards.a: IKEv1 uses two phases and optional aggressive mode; IKEv2 uses a single exchange, no aggressive mode, supports PSK or cert auth, and is simpler and more secure.

cards.q: What does an IPsec transform set specify?
cards.a: Encryption such as esp-aes, integrity such as esp-sha256, the DH group (e.g. 14 or 19), tunnel mode, and optional PFS.

cards.q: What is the classic IPsec transform set combination?
cards.a: esp-aes (encryption) combined with esp-sha (integrity), a common pair used for site-to-site VPNs.

cards.q: How does an ACL define interesting traffic in IPsec?
cards.a: The ACL matches the traffic that the tunnel carries: permitted traffic is protected, denied traffic goes clear text, and the ACL must mirror symmetrically on both sides.

cards.q: What does a crypto map bind together?
cards.a: The crypto map binds the peer, the interesting-traffic ACL, and the transform set, then is applied to an interface.

cards.q: What commands verify IPsec phase 1 and phase 2?
cards.a: show crypto isakmp sa for phase 1, show crypto ipsec sa for phase 2, plus show crypto map and show crypto errors.

cards.q: What indicates a working IPsec VPN?
cards.a: Both phase 1 and phase 2 SAs are up and the packet/byte counters in show crypto ipsec sa are incrementing for protected traffic.

cards.q: What configuration creates an isakmp policy and transform set?
cards.a: crypto isakmp policy 10 with encr aes, authentication pre-share, group 14, and crypto ipsec transform-set TS esp-aes esp-sha256.

cards.q: What configuration defines a crypto map and applies it to an interface?
cards.a: crypto map CM 1 ipsec-isakmp with set peer 1.1.1.1, transform-set TS, and match address 100, then apply crypto map CM under interface Gi0/1.

cards.q: No phase 1 SA forms. What is the likely cause and check?
cards.a: An isakmp policy mismatch, so check show crypto isakmp sa.

cards.q: Phase 1 is up but phase 2 fails. What is the likely cause and check?
cards.a: An interesting-traffic ACL mismatch, so check with show crypto ipsec sa.

cards.q: A site-to-site VPN carries no traffic despite both SAs being up. What should you check?
cards.a: The interesting-traffic ACL and the packet counters, since no traffic matched means the ACL is wrong or not mirrored on both sides.

cards.q: The IPsec SA flaps repeatedly. What is the likely cause and check?
cards.a: A lifetime setting mismatch, so check the lifetime configuration.

cards.q: IKEv1 and IKEv2 both require two phases to establish a site-to-site VPN.
cards.a: False — IKEv1 uses two phases, but IKEv2 establishes the VPN in a single exchange.

cards.q: Which element defines what traffic an IPsec tunnel protects?
cards.a: The interesting-traffic ACL, which must be mirrored/symmetric on both sides of the tunnel.

cards.q: What summarizes a healthy site-to-site IPsec VPN?
cards.a: Both ISAKMP (phase 1) and IPsec (phase 2) SAs are up with protected-traffic byte counters increasing.
